**Surat al-Kafirun (The Disbelievers)**
Six verses, Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Say: O you who disbelieve.﴾

Know that this surah is called Surat al-Munabadhah (the Surah of Repudiation), Surat al-Ikhlas (the Surah of Sincerity), and al-Muqashqishah (the Purifying). It is related that whoever recites it has recited a quarter of the Qur'an. The reasoning behind this is that the Qur'an comprises the command to do what is commanded and the prohibition of what is forbidden, and each of these two divides into what relates to the hearts and what relates to the limbs. This surah contains the prohibition of the forbidden acts related to the actions of the heart, so it is a quarter of the Qur'an. And Allah knows best.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Say: O you who disbelieve.﴾

Know that God's saying, "Say" (qul), contains several benefits:

First: The Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to be gentle and mild in all matters, as God said: ﴿Had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you﴾, ﴿It was by a mercy from Allah that you were lenient with them﴾, ﴿Compassionate and merciful toward the believers﴾, and ﴿We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds.﴾ Then he was commanded to call to Allah in the best manner: ﴿And argue with them in the best way﴾ [al-Nahl: 125]. Since this was the case, when he addressed them with "﴿O you who disbelieve﴾", they said: How does this harshness fit with that gentleness? So the answer was: I am commanded to say these words, not that I mentioned them on my own initiative. Thus the purpose of "Say" (qul) is to affirm this meaning.

Second: When he was told: ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 214], and he loved his relatives, as God said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it except affection for kinship﴾ [al-Shura: 23], kinship and the unity of lineage acted as a barrier to showing harshness. So he was commanded to state that harshness and severity explicitly, and it was said to him: "Say" (qul).

Third: When he was told: ﴿O Messenger, deliver what has been revealed to you from your Lord; and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67], he was commanded to convey everything that was revealed to him. When God said: ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve﴾, he himself (ﷺ) transmitted this whole statement, as if he were saying: God has commanded me to convey everything revealed to me, and what was revealed to me is the entirety of His saying: ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve﴾. So I too convey it to the creation in this way.

Fourth: The disbelievers acknowledged the existence of the Creator and that He is the One who created them and provided for them, as God said: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [Luqman: 25]. A servant bears from his master what he does not bear from others. Had he (ﷺ) begun by saying: ﴿O you who disbelieve﴾, they might have supposed that this was merely the speech of Muhammad, and so they might not have borne it, and they would have harmed him. But when they heard his saying "Say", they knew that he was transmitting this harshness from the Creator of the heavens and the earth, so they bore it and their harm from it was not severe.

Fifth: The saying "Say" entails that he is a messenger from Allah. When it was said to him, "Say," this was like a fresh decree confirming his prophethood. This calls for extreme honor for the Messenger, for when a king entrusts his kingdom to one of his servants, and writes him a fresh decree every month and year, this indicates the utmost care for his position and that he intends to increase his honor and dignity every day.

Sixth: When the disbelievers said: "We will worship your God for a year, and you worship our gods for a year," it is as if he (ﷺ) said: "I will consult my God about this," and He said: ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve. I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Seventh: The disbelievers spoke evil of him, so God forbade them from that and answered them, saying: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾ [al-Kawthar: 3]. It is as if God said: "When they mention you with evil, I Myself will be the one who responds. When they mention Me with evil and attribute partners to Me, you be the one who responds: ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve. I do not worship what you worship﴾."

Eighth: They called you "cut off" (abtar). If you wish to take retribution from them, then mention them with a description of blame that is true of them: ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve﴾. However, the difference is that they reproached you for what is not of your doing, while you censure them for what is their own doing.

Ninth: Suppose you say: "O you who disbelieve, I do not worship what you worship," and the disbelievers say: "Is this the speech of your Lord or your own speech? If it is the speech of your Lord, then your Lord says: 'I do not worship these idols,' and we do not seek this worship from your Lord; we seek it from you. And if this is your speech, then you said on your own: 'I do not worship these idols,' so why do you say that your Lord is the One who commanded you to do so?" But when He said "Say," this objection falls away, because the saying "Say" indicates that he is commanded by Allah, exalted is He, not to worship them and to disavow them.

Tenth: Had He revealed His saying "O you who disbelieve" without "Say," he would surely have recited it to them, for it is not permissible for him to betray the revelation. But when He said "Say," this was like an emphasis on the obligation to convey this revelation to them. Emphasis indicates that the matter is a grave one. Thus by this means this word indicates that what they said and asked of the Messenger is a matter that is abhorrent in the extreme and utterly shameful.

Eleventh: It is as if God says: "Dissimulation (taqiyyah) was permitted when one fears. But now, since We have strengthened your heart by Our saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾ [al-Kawthar: 1], and by Our saying: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, do not worry about them, do not heed them, and ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve. I do not worship what you worship﴾."

Twelfth: God's address to the servant without an intermediary entails honor. Do you not see that among the forms of humiliation of the disbelievers, God mentions that He will not speak to them? So had He said: "O you who disbelieve," this would be, insofar as it is a direct address, something that entails honor, and insofar as it describes them as disbelievers, it entails harm. The harm is compensated by honor. But when He said "Say: O you who disbelieve," the honor of being addressed reverts to Muhammad (ﷺ), and the humiliation that results for them from being described as disbelievers reverts to the disbelievers. Thus in it there is the exaltation of the friends and the humiliation of the enemies, and that is the utmost in goodness.

Thirteenth: Muhammad (ﷺ) was one of them, and he was extremely compassionate toward them and tender with them. They knew of him that he was exceedingly careful to avoid lying. A father who is extremely affectionate toward his child, and who is in the utmost truthfulness and far from lying, then describes his child with a great fault: if the child is sensible, he knows that his father described him thus, despite his extreme affection for him, only because it is true; and because he has reached a state that he cannot conceal. So God said: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to them: ﴿O you who disbelieve﴾, so that they would know that when you described them thus, despite your extreme compassion toward them and your extreme care to avoid lying, they indeed possess this ugly attribute. Perhaps this would become a motive for them to disavow this attribute and to refrain from it.

Fourteenth: Harm and alienation from one's own kin are more severe and harder than from others. You are of their tribe, and you grew up among them. So say to them: ﴿O you who disbelieve﴾, for perhaps that speech will weigh heavily upon them, and it will become a motive for them to investigate, to reflect, and to disavow disbelief.

Fifteenth: It is as if God says: "Did We not make clear in the surah ﴿By time﴾, ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and advise each other to truth and advise each other to patience﴾ [al-'Asr: 2-3]? And in the surah al-Kawthar: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, and you have brought faith and righteous deeds, in accordance with Our saying: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾ [al-Kawthar: 2]. There remains for you the advising to truth and the advising to patience, and that is to prevent them, by your tongue and your proof, from worshipping other than Allah. So say: ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve. I do not worship what you worship﴾."

Sixteenth: It is as if God says: "O Muhammad, have you forgotten that when I delayed the revelation to you for a short period, the disbelievers said: 'Your Lord has bid you farewell and forsaken you.' This distressed you exceedingly, until I sent down the surah and swore by ﴿the morning brightness﴾ and ﴿the night when it grows still﴾ [al-Duha: 1-2] that ﴿your Lord has not bid you farewell, nor has He forsaken you﴾ [al-Duha: 3]. So when you could not bear that I should leave you for a month, and your heart was not at ease until I proclaimed throughout the world that ﴿your Lord has not bid you farewell, nor has He forsaken you﴾, would you then permit that I leave you for a month while you occupy yourself with worshipping their gods? When I proclaimed the negation of that accusation, then you too proclaim throughout the world the negation of this accusation: ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve. I do not worship what you worship﴾."

* * *

Seventeenth: When they asked him to worship their gods for a year and they would worship his God for a year, he (ﷺ) remained silent and said nothing. This was not because he entertained in his heart the possibility that what they said was true, for he was certain of the falsehood of what they said. Rather, he (ﷺ) hesitated over how to answer them: Should he do so by presenting rational proofs against that? Or by repelling them with the sword? Or by asking God to send down a punishment upon them? The disbelievers seized upon that silence and said: "Muhammad has inclined toward our religion." So it is as if God said: "O Muhammad, your hesitation in answering is, in reality, correct, but it gave rise to a falsehood. So hasten to remove that falsehood, and declare what is the truth: ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve. I do not worship what you worship﴾."

Eighteenth: When his Lord said to him on the night of the Mi'raj (Ascension): "Praise Me," he was overcome by awe of the Divine Presence, and said: "I cannot enumerate praise of You." That silence on his part was in the utmost beauty. So it is as if it was said to him: "If you remained silent from praise out of reverence for the Divine Presence, then loose your tongue in censure of the enemies: ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve﴾, so that your silence is for Allah and your speech is for Allah." There is also another interpretation in this: the awe of the Presence deprived you of the power of speech, so speak here, so that the awe of your speech may deprive these disbelievers of the power of speech.

Nineteenth: Had He said to him, "Do not worship what they worship," it would not have necessarily followed that he should say with his tongue: "I do not worship what you worship." But when He commanded him to say with his tongue: "I do not worship what you worship," it follows that he must not worship what they worship, for if he did so, his speech would become a lie. Thus it is established that when He said to him "Say: I do not worship what you worship," it became binding on him to be a rejecter of that in his heart, tongue and limbs. Had He said to him, "Do not worship what they worship," it would have obliged him to abstain, but it would not have obliged him to make his rejection manifest by tongue. It is well known that the utmost rejection is achieved only when one abandons it in oneself and rejects it with one's tongue. So His saying to him "Say" entails extreme emphasis on rejection, and for this reason He said: "Say: ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾."

Twentieth: The mention of monotheism (tawhid) and the negation of rivals is a paradise for the knowers and a fire for the polytheists. So make your utterance a paradise for the monotheists and a fire for the polytheists: ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve. I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Twenty-first: When the disbelievers said, "We will worship your God for a year, and you worship our gods for a year," Muhammad fell silent. He said: "If I confront them with rejection, they will be harmed, and aversion to Islam will arise in their hearts." So it is as if God said to him: "O Muhammad, why did you remain silent from rejecting them? As for the hope of what they promise you, that they will accept your religion, you have no need of them in this regard: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾. As for fear of them, We have removed it from you by Our saying: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾. So do not heed them, and do not care about their speech: ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve. I do not worship what you worship﴾."

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 109, verse 1 (part 2 of 3):

Twenty-second: Have you forgotten, O Muhammad, that I placed your right above My own right? So I said: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists were not going to desist﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 1]. Thus I put the People of the Scripture before the polytheists in disbelief, because the People of the Scripture defame you and the polytheists defame Me. So I placed your right above My right, and I placed the People of the Scripture before the polytheists in censure. You too used to act this way: when they broke your tooth, you said: "O Allah, guide my people," and when they distracted you from prayer on the day of the Trench, you said: "O Allah, fill their bellies with fire." So here too, place My right above your own right. Whether you fear them or do not fear them, make plain your rejection of their saying: ﴿Say: O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Twenty-third: It is as if He, exalted is He, says: The affair of Zayd's wife is a trivial matter compared with this affair. Moreover, there I was not content with you concealing in your heart something you did not express with your tongue. Rather I said to you, by way of reproach: ﴿And you concealed within yourself what Allah was to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you should fear Him﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37]. If I was not content with you in that trivial affair except with declaration and with disregarding the sayings of people, how then could I be content with you in this matter, which is the greatest of matters in importance, with silence? Say with the clear expression of your tongue: ﴿O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Twenty-fourth: O Muhammad, did I not say to you: ﴿Had We willed, We would have sent a warner to every town﴾ [al-Furqan: 51]? Yet with this power, I cared for your side, comforted your heart, and proclaimed among the worlds that I do not make the prophethood shared between Him and another. Rather, the prophethood belongs to him alone and to no other, when I said: ﴿But the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40]. So you, knowing that it is rationally impossible for anyone else to share in My being worshipped, are more deserving of proclaiming the negation of this partnership among the worlds. So say: ﴿O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Twenty-fifth: It is as if He, exalted is He, says: These people came to you and hoped that you would follow them and that you would follow their religion, so you kept silent about denunciation and refutation. Did I not make the pledge with you a pledge with Me, when I said: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are only pledging allegiance to Allah﴾ [al-Fath: 10]? And did I not make following you a following of Me, when I said: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 31]? Then I proclaimed among the worlds and said: ﴿That Allah is free of the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾ [al-Tawbah: 3]. So you too must declare this clearly, and say: ﴿Say: O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Twenty-sixth: It is as if He, exalted is He, says: Am I not more merciful to you than a father is to his son? Moreover, nakedness and hunger with a father are better than satiety with strangers. How much more so, when the hunger is for them, because their idols are hungry of life, naked of attributes, while they themselves are hungry for knowledge and naked of piety. So you have tested Me. Did I not find you an orphan and give you refuge? Did I not find you lost and guide you? Did I not find you poor and enrich you? Did We not expand your breast? Did I not give you, through al-Siddiq, a treasury, through al-Faruq, awe, through 'Uthman, assistance, and through 'Ali, knowledge? Did I not protect you from the People of the Elephant when they sought to destroy your city? Did I not protect your forefathers on the journey of winter and summer? Did I not give you al-Kawthar? Did I not guarantee that your enemy is cut off? Did your grandfather not say, after these idols had been destroyed: ﴿Why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees, and which does not avail you anything?﴾ [Maryam: 42]. So declare your disavowal of them, and say: ﴿O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

* * *

Twenty-seventh: It is as if He, exalted is He, says: O Muhammad, did I not send down to you: ﴿Remember Allah as you remember your fathers, or with even greater remembrance﴾ [al-Baqarah: 200]?

Moreover, if someone attributed you to parents other than your own, you would be angry, you would show denial, and you would exaggerate in it, to the point where you said: "I was born of a lawful marriage and I was not born of fornication." So if you did not remain silent when partners were associated in your birth, how could you remain silent when partners are associated in worship? Rather, show denial and emphasize it clearly, and say: ﴿O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Twenty-eighth: It is as if He, exalted is He, says: O Muhammad, did I not send down to you: ﴿Is then He who creates like one who does not create? Will you not then remember?﴾ [al-Nahl: 17]. Thus I ruled that whoever equates the Creator God with a lifeless idol in worship is not rational but insane. Moreover, I swore and said: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe. You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman﴾ [al-Qalam: 1-3]. The disbelievers say that you are mad. So declare the rejection of their saying, for it establishes My innocence of the defect of associating partners and your innocence of the defect of madness. And say: ﴿O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Twenty-ninth: These disbelievers named the idols "gods," but sharing a name does not necessitate sharing a meaning. Do you not see that a man and a woman share humanity in reality, yet all guardianship (qayyimiyyah) belongs to the husband, because he is more knowledgeable and more capable? And whoever is more knowledgeable and more capable has all the right to guardianship. So how can one who has no power and no knowledge at all have any right to self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah)? Moreover, there is another matter: if a woman were claimed by two men and they reached an agreement over her, that is not permissible. If each of them produced evidence that she is his wife, neither would be adjudged her husband, and a slave-girl owned by two persons is not lawful to either of them. So if it is not permissible for one woman to belong to two husbands, nor for one slave-girl to be shared by two masters in lawful intercourse, how is it conceivable for one worshipper to be between two objects of worship? Indeed, whoever permits two spouses to agree that the wife be lawful to one of them for a month, and then to the other for another month, would be an unbeliever. So whoever permits a compromise between God and an idol, is he not a disbeliever? It is as if He, exalted is He, says to His Messenger: This statement is utterly ugly, so declare your denial plainly and say: ﴿O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Thirtieth: It is as if He, exalted is He, says: Have you forgotten that when I gave your wives a choice, when I sent down to you: ﴿Say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment…﴾ [al-Ahzab: 28], up to His words: ﴿a great reward﴾ [al-Ahzab: 29]? Then you feared that 'A'ishah might choose the worldly life, so you said to her: "Do not say anything until you consult your parents." She said: "Am I to consult my parents about this? Rather I choose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode!" So a deficient-minded one did not hesitate in what opposes My pleasure, but do you hesitate in what opposes My pleasure and My command? Yet I am the Compeller of the heavens and the earth. So say: ﴿O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Thirty-first: It is as if He, exalted is He, says: O Muhammad, are you not the one who said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not place himself in situations of suspicion"? Indeed, some shaykhs said to a disciple who wished to leave him: "Do not fear the sultan." He said: "Why?" He said: "Because he places people in one of two errors: either they believe the sultan is pious, because the ascetic scholar associates with him, or they believe you are a sinner like him. Both are errors." So if it is established that one must dissociate from situations of suspicion, then your silence, O Muhammad, regarding this statement draws upon you the accusation of approval of it, especially since it has already occurred that Satan cast, in the midst of your recitation: "Those are the exalted cranes, whose intercession is hoped for." So remove this accusation from yourself, and say: ﴿O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Thirty-second: Rights in the case of a witness are of two kinds: the right of the one under your hand, who is your master, and the right of the one under your authority, who is the child. Then we all agree that serving the master takes precedence over raising the child. So if the right of the metaphorical master takes precedence, then it is even more fitting that the right of the true Master takes precedence. It was also narrated that 'Ali, peace be upon him, asked the Messenger ﷺ for permission to marry the daughter of Abu Jahl, and he became displeased and said: "I do not permit it, I do not permit it, I do not permit it. Fatimah is a part of me; what troubles her troubles me, and what pleases her pleases me. By Allah, the daughter of the enemy of Allah and the daughter of the beloved of Allah shall not be combined." So it is as if He, exalted is He, says: You declared the refusal there and repeated it emphatically, out of regard for the right of the child. So here it is even more fitting that you declare the refusal and repeat it, out of regard for the right of the Master. So say: ﴿O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾, and do not combine in the heart obedience to the Beloved and obedience to the enemy.

Thirty-third: O Muhammad, did you not say to 'Umar: "I saw a palace in Paradise. I said: 'For whom is it?' It was said: 'For a young man of Quraysh.' I said: 'Who is it?' They said: ''Umar.' So I feared your jealousy and did not enter it until 'Umar said: 'Would I be jealous of you, O Messenger of Allah?'" So it is as if He, exalted is He, said: You feared the jealousy of 'Umar, so you did not enter his palace. Do you not fear My jealousy, that the obedience of another might enter your heart? Moreover, there you showed refusal, so here too show refusal, and say: ﴿O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Thirty-fourth: Do you think My favor upon you is less than the favor of your mother? Did I not nurture you? Did I not create you? Did I not provide for you? Did I not give you life, power, intellect, guidance, and success? Then, when you were a child without reason, and you recognized the upbringing of your mother, if a woman more beautiful, more graceful, and more noble than your mother had taken you, you would have shown aversion and wept, and if she had offered you her breast, you would have closed your mouth, saying: "I want no one but my mother, because she is the first to bestow favor upon me." So here it is even more fitting that you show aversion and say: "I worship none but my Lord, because He is the first to bestow favor upon me." So say: ﴿O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Thirty-fifth: The favor of feeding is less than the favor of reason and prophethood. Moreover, you know that a sheep and a dog do not forget the favor of feeding, nor do they incline to anyone other than the one who fed them. So how is it fitting for a rational person to forget the favor of bringing into existence and of beneficence? How much more so regarding the best of creation: ﴿Say: O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Thirty-sixth: The doctrine of al-Shafi'i is that the right of separation is established through inability to provide maintenance (nafaqah). So if you did not find from the Helpers any upbringing, I would have granted you the right of separation, had you been connected to them. ﴿Why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees, and which does not avail you anything﴾. Thus, supposing you had been connected to them, it would have been obligatory for you to disconnect from them and leave them. How much more so, when you were not connected to them! Is it fitting for you to seek closeness to them? ﴿Say: O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Thirty-seventh: These disbelievers, out of extreme foolishness, supposed that plurality in divinity is like plurality in wealth, by which one becomes richer. But the matter is not so; rather it is like plurality of dependents, by which one's need increases. So say, O Muhammad: "I have one God, for whom I stand in the night and fast in the day. Yet I have not finished fulfilling the right of even one atom of His blessings. So how could I bind myself to worshipping many gods?" ﴿Say: O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Thirty-eighth: When Gabriel, peace be upon him, appeared to Mary, peace be upon her, she said: ﴿I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing﴾ [Maryam: 18]. She sought refuge lest she incline toward Gabriel instead of God. So do you, with your complete manhood, think it permissible to incline toward idols? ﴿Say: O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

Thirty-ninth: The doctrine of Abu Hanifa is that the right of separation is not established by inability to provide maintenance, nor by subsequent impotence (al-'unnah). He says: Because she was a spouse, it is not fitting to turn away from her, even though he has become defective. So the True One, glorified is He, says: "I was a Guardian, and I did not become defective. So how is it permissible to turn away from Me?" ﴿Say: O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾.

The fortieth: These disbelievers acknowledged that Allah is their Creator. He says, ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ [Luqman: 25] And in another place He says, ﴿Show me what they have created from the earth.﴾ [Fatir: 40] So it is as if the Exalted is saying: This partnership is either a *muzara'a* (sharecropping partnership, in which one party supplies land and another labour), and that is false, because the seed is from Me, the cultivation and watering are from Me, and the guarding is from Me, so what is left for the idol? Or it is a *shirkat al-wujuh* (partnership based on credit and reputation), and that is also false. Do you think the idol is more famous and more manifest than Me? Or it is a *shirkat al-abdan* (partnership of labour), and that is also false, because that requires a shared kind (*jinsiyya*) between the partners. Or it is a *shirkat al-inan* (partnership of capital), and that is also false, because it requires a minimum amount (*nisab*). So what is the *nisab* of the idols? Or one may say: this is not a case of partnership at all, but the idol takes by force and domination a share of the dominion. Then the Lord says: How great is your ignorance! This idol is weaker than a fly: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly.﴾ [al-Hajj: 73] I create the seed and then cast it into the earth; the cultivation, watering and guarding are from Me. Then one who is weaker than a fly takes by compulsion and domination a share from Me! This is not a statement fitting for sensible people. So: ﴿Say, "O disbelievers,"﴾ ﴿"I do not worship what you worship."﴾

The forty-first: There is not a single atom in the world of created things but that it calls minds to knowledge of the Essence and the Attributes. As for those who call to knowledge of the commands of Allah, they are the Prophets, peace be upon them. Since every gnat and mosquito calls to knowledge of the Essence and Attributes, He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example, [even] of a mosquito or what is above it.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 26] This is because this mosquito, according to the createdness of its essence and attributes, calls to the power of Allah; according to its wondrous composition, it calls to the knowledge of Allah; and according to the specification of its essence and attributes with a particular measure, it calls to the will of Allah. So it is as if the Exalted is saying: How can one be ashamed of such a thing? It is narrated that 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, during his caliphate entered the market, bought a tripe, and carried it himself. 'Ali saw him from afar and moved aside from the road. Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 109, verse 2–5:

As for His saying, ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾ ﴿nor will you worship what I worship﴾ ﴿nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped﴾ ﴿nor will you be worshippers of what I worship﴾:

There are several issues concerning this.

The first issue: concerning this verse there are two opinions.

One of them: there is no repetition in it.

The second: there is repetition in it. As for the first, its explanation is from several aspects:

The first aspect: the first clause refers to the future, and the second refers to the present. The evidence that the first refers to the future is that "lā" (not) only enters upon a present-tense verb that carries the meaning of the future. Observe that "lan" (never) is an emphatic form of what "lā" negates, and al-Khalil said about "lan": its origin is "lā an." Once this is established, His saying ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾ means: I will not, in the future, do what you ask of me in the worship of your gods, and you will not, in the future, do what I ask of you in the worship of my God. Then He said: ﴿nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped﴾, meaning: nor am I, at present, a worshipper of what you worship, nor are you, at present, worshippers of what my God is worshipped by.

The second aspect: you reverse the matter, making the first refer to the present and the second refer to the future. The evidence that His saying ﴿nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped﴾ refers to the future is that it is raised in response to the sense of our saying: "I am a worshipper of what you worship." We say: as for the narration about himself, it is so that the ignorant person does not imagine that he worships them secretly, out of fear of them or desire for them. As for His negation of their worship, it is because the act of the disbeliever is not worship at all.

There are several issues concerning this.

The first issue: concerning this verse there are two opinions.

One of them: there is no repetition in it.

The second: there is repetition in it. As for the first, its explanation is from several aspects:

The first aspect: the first clause refers to the future, and the second refers to the present. The second aspect: you reverse the matter, making the first refer to the present and the second refer to the future. The evidence that His saying ﴿nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped﴾ refers to the future is that it is raised in response to the sense of our saying: "I am a worshipper of what you worship." Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 109, verse 6:

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾, there are several issues.

The first issue: Ibn 'Abbas said: "For you is your disbelief in Allah, and for me is the tawhid (monotheism) and sincere devotion to Him." If it is asked: "Is it said that He permitted them to disbelieve?" We say: No. For indeed, peace be upon him, was sent only to prevent disbelief, so how would he permit it? Rather, the intended meaning is one of several matters:

The first of them: that the intended meaning is a threat, like His saying: "Do what you will."

The second of them: it is as though he is saying: "I am a Prophet sent to you to call you to the truth and to salvation. So if you do not accept from me and do not follow me, then leave me and do not call me to polytheism."

The third of them: ﴿For you is your religion﴾, so remain upon it if destruction is good for you; ﴿and for me is my religion﴾, because I do not abandon it.

The second opinion regarding the interpretation of the verse: that the religion here means the reckoning, i.e., for you is your reckoning and for me is my reckoning, and no effect of one another's deeds returns to either of us at all.

The third opinion: that it is according to the omission of a modifier, i.e., for you is the recompense of your religion and for me is the recompense of my religion; and their recompense is, for them, ruin and punishment, just as your recompense for your religion is, for you, honour and reward.

The fourth opinion: religion means punishment: ﴿And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah﴾ [an-Nur: 2], meaning the prescribed penalty. So for you is punishment from my Lord, and for me is punishment from your idols. But your idols are inanimate, so I do not fear the punishment of idols. As for you, it is rationally fitting for you to fear the punishment of the Mighty One of the heavens and the earth.

The fifth opinion: religion means supplication. So call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion; i.e., for you is your supplication. ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 14]. ﴿If you call them, they will not hear your call, and even if they heard, they would not respond to you﴾ [Fatir: 14]. Then, would that they remained in this state so that they would not harm you; rather, on the Day of Resurrection they will find a tongue and disown your polytheism. As for my Lord, He says: ﴿And He responds to those who believe﴾ [ash-Shura: 26], ﴿Call upon Me; I will respond to you﴾ [Ghafir: 60], ﴿I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 186].

The sixth opinion: religion means custom. The poet said:

He says to her, when my saddle-girth has turned: "Is this her religion forever, and my religion?"

Its meaning: for you is your custom, which is taken from your forefathers and from the devils, and for me is my custom, which is taken from the angels and revelation. Then each of us remains upon his custom until you meet the devils and the Fire, and I meet the angels and the Garden.

The second issue: His saying, ﴿For you is your religion﴾, implies restriction (ḥaṣr), and its meaning is: for you is your religion, not for others; and for me is my religion, not for others. It is an indication of His saying: ﴿And that man has only what he strives for﴾ [an-Najm: 39], and ﴿No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ [al-An'am: 164]. That is, I am commanded with revelation and conveying, and you are commanded with compliance and acceptance. So when I have done what I was charged with, I have discharged the obligation of the charge. As for your persistence in your disbelief, no harm whatsoever returns to me from it.

The second issue (another): It has become the custom of people to recite this verse at the time of parting, and that is impermissible, because Allah, Exalted is He, did not send down the Qur'an to be recited as a formula, but to be reflected upon, and then acted upon according to its requirement. And Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, knows best and is most wise. And may Allah bless our master Muhammad, and his family and companions, and grant them peace.
